findings.issue: The confinement assertion compares resolved paths with case-sensitive string equality. On Windows, a legitimate direct-child target whose directory spelling differs only by case is rejected with EOUTOFSTORE, despite resolving to the same directory.
findings.repro: Created a temp store named StoreCase, verified its uppercase spelling had identical dev/ino and identical realpath, then called atomicWriteInStore(actualStore, UPPERCASE_STORE\\case.md, data). It threw EOUTOFSTORE and created no target.
findings.fix: Use a platform-aware path identity comparison, such as path.relative(resolvedStore, path.dirname(resolvedTarget)) === '', which treats case according to the current platform while retaining lexical direct-child confinement.

findings.issue: strayTempNames() swallows every readdirSync failure as an empty result. The apply path can therefore discard an I/O error and subsequently report a successful clean mutation—the same failure-discarded-then-success shape as the prior close defect.
findings.repro: In a valid temp store, injected EIO only when readdirSync was called from strayTempNames(), then ran a valid correct plan. run() returned {ok:true,fatal:false,applied:true}, wrote the new body, and reported the post-check clean.
findings.fix: Do not convert readdir errors to []; propagate the error or return a fatal result so inability to perform the stray-temp scan cannot be reported as a successful apply.
